scope: Six assigned PairFree files only. These describe host-side accessory commands, not recovered Bluetooth controller HCI, LMP, or LLCP handlers. No VM, hardware, network, or Ghidra analysis occurred.

findings.claim: The repository documents research from Skullcandy 5.0.6. It reports no Skullcandy implementation and no connected hardware.
findings.model_scope: All Skullcandy research in these four documents

findings.claim: Crusher PLYR 720 has product id 0x29 and model S6PCW. Crusher PLYR 720 XBOX has product id 0x2A and model S6PXW. Both catalog entries select bluetoothClassic and leAudio.
findings.model_scope: Crusher PLYR 720 and Crusher PLYR 720 XBOX

findings.claim: Both catalog entries include mic gain, sidetone, clear voice, Crusher bass boost, Crusher controls, customEqualizer4x, presets, enhanced sound perception, game/chat mix, gaming EQ, LED settings, multipoint, THX headtracking, and THX spatial audio. These are unions across firmware entries.
findings.model_scope: Crusher PLYR 720 and Crusher PLYR 720 XBOX

findings.claim: Android connection types do not identify command protocols. The app contains legacy BLE, GAIA, RACE, JieLi, and Bragi paths. A model name alone does not select a path.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: The documented frame is 7E FF flags protocol length_u16_BE header_CRC8 payload optional_FCS_u16_BE. The seven-byte header includes its CRC. Normal flags are 0x80 when the FCS is present.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: The payload selectors are 0x90 user plane, 0x91 RTP, 0x92 secure RTP, 0x93 protobuf, 0x94 BOS-RPC, and 0x95 secure BOS-RPC.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: Header CRC-8/ROHC uses reflected polynomial 0xE0, initial 0xFF, no final XOR, over bytes 0..5. CRC-16/MCRF4XX uses reflected polynomial 0x8408, initial 0xFFFF, no final XOR, over header bytes 1..6 and payload. The FCS is stored high byte first.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: The reader accepts partial headers, partial payloads, multiple frames, and split FCS bytes. Its internal buffer holds 4096 bytes. Oversized announced lengths need explicit rejection in a new implementation.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: Some serializers pass an RPC body through another framing layer. Other serializers add PPP directly. The selected transport must determine the wrapping.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: The plaintext RPC body starts with flags/type, service, method, and tag bytes. Type uses bits 2..3: request 0, response 1, status 2, abort 3. The serializer sets final flag 0x10. Replies require tag, service, and method matching.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: A STATUS body must contain zero in its first byte for success under the documented vendor implementation. An empty body does not explicitly indicate success. Status 0x64 means that another subscription replaced the subscription.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: The device.dev_info frame 7E FF 80 94 00 06 2D 10 02 01 00 08 00 54 80 is an analytical vector. It is not a hardware capture and does not prove authentication.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: Service 25 handles authenticated access. device.dev_info field 12 reports its requirement. The SDK contains ECDH and AES-GCM, AES-CCM, and ChaCha20-Poly1305 paths. No secure session or pairing was attempted.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: The secure-session evidence describes local accessory communication. It does not establish whether the firmware package is encrypted or identify a firmware key.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: The Java helper uses 05 5A for requests, 05 5B for replies, and 05 5D for notifications. It uses a little-endian 16-bit length and a command id. The SDK timeout is 8000 milliseconds. These files do not supply the complete RACE layout.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: The Dart snapshot exposes strings for Crusher EQ volume, spatial audio, headtracking, LEDs, and other features. Strings do not establish command ids or model-to-chip mapping.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: The Skullcandy libnative-peq.so hash is ffa603fecd3e496a12c5b1f541b56b2c83566801f19200db9ed92cc27bb0ee68. NativePeq_getCofeParam was inspected at 0x1C2A4. This does not prove compatibility with the existing PairFree coefficient implementation.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: AirohaPeq implements math derived from JBL Headphones 5.37.10. PEQ takes bandwidth in Hz, but SERIALIZE takes Q. Supported sample rates are 32000, 44100, 48000, 88200, and 96000 Hz.
findings.model_scope: JBL-derived Airoha math; Crusher PLYR 720 compatibility unverified

findings.claim: The implementation returns 3 + 10 * band_count shorts. It starts with the band count. Each stage contains five 32-bit coefficients split into high and low shorts. The final 32-bit master gain uses Q26.
findings.model_scope: JBL-derived Airoha math; Crusher PLYR 720 compatibility unverified

findings.claim: The test code compares coefficients and peak values with JBL library vectors. It requires at least 30 cases. These tests are not Skullcandy device captures, and this analysis did not execute them.
findings.model_scope: JBL-derived Airoha math; Crusher PLYR 720 compatibility unverified

findings.claim: The virtual test used Crusher 1080 ANC, not PLYR 720. The app displayed Internet Required. No RFCOMM control channel or application command was captured.
findings.model_scope: Crusher 1080 ANC only

findings.claim: 54C5BF4C-C52F-4635-98DC-EEBF97C6726F is a Bragi service lead attributed to the untested Earshot Crusher 1080 notes. A4602B24-... is a separate Airoha service lead. Neither identifies the PLYR 720 service in these files.
findings.model_scope: Crusher 1080 ANC reference only

findings.claim: Bragi service 23 exposes config_get 1, state_get 2, and state_set 3. The config reports maximum intensity, an intensity read-only flag, and optional mode count. The set fields are optional active, intensity, and mode. Modes 0/1/2 mean high/medium/low only where supported.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: Hearing mode configuration uses protobuf fields mode 1, activate 2, optional preset 3, and optional gain 4. The schema warns that Airoha can delay acoustic application by 500 milliseconds. Unsolicited state can precede the reply.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified

findings.claim: Bragi EQ uses frequency, floating gain, and Q. Device limits specify band count, ranges, and quantization. Its protobuf fields cannot be replaced with native coefficients without compatibility evidence.
findings.model_scope: Skullcandy Android 5.0.6 SDK; applicability to Crusher PLYR 720 unverified
